canonical_delivery.selection: one_shot must bypass shared/per-sender session selection; use one_shot_calls plus the single-use slot claimed for the domain operation
canonical_delivery.call_identity: Stable logical delivery operation ID, not dispatch attempt ID. Broadcast destinations already have independent delivery operations.
canonical_delivery.authorization: Keep validate_domain_delivery and canonical resolve/admit/lease gates; a pool reservation is never a grant.
canonical_delivery.queue: Commit logical call and queue admission in the message write transaction. Do not reserve a productive runtime operation until a slot is available.
canonical_delivery.rejection: Expose capacity refusal in the synchronous caller response and preserve per-recipient results for fanout.
canonical_delivery.warm_scope: Pool matching includes agent, executor, workspace/binding, approved launch configuration, harness settings and preset revision; never consume a warm instance prepared for another workspace.
canonical_delivery.dispatch: Record possible productive dispatch before the native write; do not infer absence of effects from missing receipts. Retry only with existing canonical unsent proofs.

controller.integration: Runtime owner scan, bounded per-host work, isolated failures; use canonical runtime.start/runtime.close and current lease authority.
controller.ordering: Reconcile host facts, settle terminal outcomes, expire deadlines, dispose closing resources, serve queues, then replenish idle capacity.
controller.durability: Call success must match final event and receipt. Persist caller outcome before requesting close; a cleanup failure cannot overwrite it.
controller.recovery: Host-owned process birth/journal evidence must confirm resource release. Never delete slot on disconnect, timeout or session terminal label alone.
controller.availability: Normal one-shot closure is expected resource lifecycle and does not revoke the agent binding or trigger agent-wide Recovering.
controller.limits: Host cap must also account for non-one-shot native resources without double-counting canonical sessions attached to slots.

mcp_launch.snapshot: Bind structured preset and revision/digest to the signed opening payload, Core preparation fingerprint and receipt binding. Negotiate support explicitly with old Connectors.
mcp_launch.secrets: Use executor-local approved references; do not put resolved secrets into CLI arguments, wire payloads, events or the public configuration.
mcp_launch.composition: Inherited configuration, whole-entry preset replacement/disable, then reserved Nexus integration. Codex recursive native table merge needs explicit isolation; dictionary composition alone does not prove removal of inherited credential fields.
mcp_launch.pi: Implement an application-owned MCP client bridge into the Pi tool injection path with per-tool authorization, namespacing and session-owned cleanup. Existing Core helper intentionally refuses native Pi MCP rendering.
mcp_launch.updates: New sessions use the new snapshot; running calls keep their snapshot. Retire unused incompatible warm instances without modifying global harness files.
mcp_launch.reset: Preserve preset/limit configuration when preserving agents and runtime configuration; reconcile outstanding calls/resources under reset semantics.

next_steps: Apply the validated development wheels to the user instance for operator acceptance; current process was intentionally preserved.
Publication is a separate requested action.

resource_pool.domain: PoolPolicy, PoolRequest and PoolInstance: no SQL, Core or framework imports.
resource_pool.ports: PoolTransaction composes RequestQueue and InstancePool in one serializable transaction. Caller owns commit/rollback and execution outbox atomicity.
resource_pool.internal_adapters: SQLiteRequestQueue and SQLiteInstancePool retain existing tables and history; composition root selects adapters.
resource_pool.distribution: Future infrastructure adapter must provide serializable admission, stable request identity, no independent dequeue acknowledgement, durable caller outcomes and fenced correlated disposal; do not substitute an unfenced expiring cache lock.
resource_pool.allocation: Pool is keyed by agent; resource matching also requires host and configuration digest. Starting, warm, claimed, running and closing all count. max_parallel=0 means no pool-specific ceiling, still constrained by host. ADMITTED can reserve capacity without an instance; only WARM resources are assigned, FIFO among compatible waiters. STARTING instances are shared preparation, never productive request affinity. Legacy already-bound sessions retain their effect fences.
resource_pool.queue: Bounded queue, FIFO within pool/host, interleaved pool scanning, immediate capacity rejection or durable wait expiry. Expired requests are never dispatched.
resource_pool.dispatch: Reserve the full warm deficit in one pass; independent asynchronous native opens. Server opening window 28 plus four ready submissions stays within 32 productive wire credits; shared byte credit is retained. Connector opening workers follow its host session budget; controls retain independent workers. Both hosts default to 64 physical slots, including preparing and closing resources.
resource_pool.failures: One outcome per request, no capacity release before disposal, no automatic replay after possible execution, warm failure backoff per pool/host.
resource_pool.scope: Reusable single-use resource service, applied to all runtime harnesses and local/remote delivery. Existing shared/per-sender affinity remains unchanged.
resource_pool.connector: Bounded transport reservations retained across independent producers; separate semaphores for startup/ready/control. Preparing sessions reserve host capacity before the first await.
